replies.author: YiyaK
replies.text:
In the beginning after installation, I would GO SLOW. I wasted a lot of time over the past couple of weeks installing, uninstalling, and rearranging things. Graphene provides everything needed for a functional user experience, right from the beginning.

I took some some time to read (and reread) the user guide. A lot of stuff there was over my head, but a lot wasn't, and I learned where things are and what they do. Graphene is a highly customizable OS - I just need to keep reminding myself that, as a normie, I don't need a lot of that customization. But now I know where to find out how to go about it is I decide I do at some later time.

I downloaded almost everything initially from the Graphene app store. I left the Google options alone at first, and still haven't bothered with the note feature.

Also, I downloaded the f-droid store from their website: https://f-droid.org/ to have more app options and to reload some of my favorites.

The keyboard was driving me crazy - I need Swipe typing capability - so I downloaded the FUTO keyboard from the Obtainium store. I'm still figuring Obtainium out, BTW.

I downloaded the Signal messaging app from the f-droid store. It's also available directly from their website: https://f-droid.org/

That was enough customization for day one - the open source basics I know and was already using, set up to Graphene OS.

I started here in the Graphene forum on day one, also. Lots of helpful folks here, though some suggestions and answers to my questions are a bit techie for me. I'm learning, though!

replies.author: YiyaK
replies.text:
Another thing I struggled with was whether or not I needed a VPN - I wasn't really sure what a VPN did. Found an excellent summary at the IVPN site, here: https://www.ivpn.net/en/

Scroll down to the "Do I really need a VPN" section.

I decided that I don't want my internet/cellular provider tracking which websites I visit, don't want websites tracking my IP address when I visit them, and, in the rare event I use public WiFi, want to keep that private too.

I'm using the free Proton VPN service for now - it meets my basic needs.

replies.author: de0u
replies.text:
YiyaK When evaluating whether or not to use a VPN, it might be useful to consult sources other than VPN providers.

Occasionally I encourage Naomi Brockwell's content (NBTV.media), because explanations are fairly clear and, though I haven't watched a lot of them, I haven't seen advice that seems genuinely bad. As it happens, she recently did a piece on potential issues with some VPNs... https://www.nbtv.media/episodes/is-the-government-running-a-dragnet-on-vpn-users

(I have no affiliation, financial or otherwise with NBTV.)

replies.author: YiyaK
replies.text: de0u I get what you're saying about sources and I read a bit before going to the site. I thought they had a clear explanation about both what a VPN can and can't do.
